_description: Knowledge base for LLM structured extraction verification, curated for MLGG extract_paper_metadata.py pipeline. Focused on document-grounded information extraction accuracy, not general chatbot hallucination.

problem_definition.task: Extract structured metadata (AUROC, sample sizes, split strategy, leakage risk) from medical ML papers into Pydantic schema
risk_types: numeric_fabrication: LLM invents values not in paper text
value_drift: LLM returns schema-invalid categorical values
inference_error: LLM makes unsupported methodology judgments (leakage risk)
omission: LLM returns null for fields clearly stated in text
problem_definition.not_the_problem: This is NOT general chatbot hallucination or medical QA — it is document-grounded structured IE

implemented_defenses.description: Pydantic Literal types reject non-allowed categorical values at parse time
model_post_init checks arithmetic consistency, CI ordering, range bounds
4 *_evidence fields require LLM to cite paper text for boolean leakage determinations
implemented_defenses.effectiveness: enables human audit; does not yet verify quotes against source

implemented_defenses.description: _llm_extracted_fields list and _source tag in mlgg_audit, downstream score_paper_metadata emits _llm_confidence_note
implemented_defenses.effectiveness: consumers can distinguish LLM vs human data

recommended_next_steps.description: Regex check: do extracted numbers (AUROC, n_patients, prevalence) actually appear in the paper text?
recommended_next_steps.evidence: SciEx verifies 'every extracted value must be traceable to its source context'. Zeba 2025 uses numerical tests against EHR records.

recommended_next_steps.description: Fuzzy match (difflib.SequenceMatcher) check: do *_evidence strings actually appear in the paper source text?
recommended_next_steps.evidence: SciEx provenance annotation requires traceability. MARCH decomposes into verifiable claims.

extraction_accuracy.consensus_3_llm: 1.48% true-error rate ≈ neurologist level (Poser 2026, 30 MS reports)
extraction_accuracy.dual_llm_concordant_accuracy: 0.94 accuracy for concordant GPT-4-turbo + Claude-3-Opus responses (JAMIA 2024)

prompt_engineering_insights: 9 rounds of prompt iteration to reach 1.48% error (Poser 2026)

papers.title: Hallucination Detection and Mitigation in Large Language Models
papers.relevance: HIGH — operational framework for hallucination in regulated document extraction (financial case study)
papers.key_takeaway: Root cause-aware detection+mitigation cycle; Table 1 maps detection methods to ground truth requirements; Table 2 compares open vs closed-weight model capabilities

papers.title: MARCH: Multi-Agent Reinforced Self-Check for LLM Hallucination
papers.relevance: MODERATE — Solver/Proposer/Checker architecture with information asymmetry
papers.key_takeaway: Claim decomposition + blinded verification pattern. Implementation requires MARL training (not practical for MLGG), but architectural concept applicable

papers.title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Healthcare LLMs with Granular Fact-Checking
papers.relevance: MODERATE — independent fact-checker concept (F1=0.8556 on MIMIC-III)
papers.key_takeaway: Decouple verification from extraction LLM to avoid self-verification bias. Numerical tests + discrete logic NLP patterns

papers.title: Improving reliability and accuracy of structured data extraction using a consensus LLM approach
papers.relevance: CRITICAL — most directly applicable method for MLGG
papers.key_takeaway: 3-LLM consensus achieves 1.48% error rate on structured clinical data extraction. 9 prompt iteration rounds. Method directly replicable

papers.title: Automation of Systematic Reviews with Large Language Models (otto-SR)
papers.key_takeaway: 93.1% extraction accuracy vs human 79.7%. Blinded adjudication resolves discrepancies. 12 Cochrane reviews in 2 days

papers.title: Exploring the Use of a Large Language Model for Data Extraction in Systematic Reviews
papers.relevance: HIGH — error pattern analysis directly maps to MLGG
papers.key_takeaway: ~80% accuracy; study design and causal inference hardest (= MLGG leakage_risk); prompt wording sensitivity documented

papers.title: Exploring LLMs for Scientific Information Extraction using the SciEx Framework
papers.relevance: CRITICAL — most architecturally similar to MLGG
papers.key_takeaway: Retrieval-Extract-Verify closed loop; provenance per value; schema-constrained decoding; self-verification triggers re-retrieval

papers.title: SciDaSynth: Interactive Structured Data Extraction from Scientific Literature with LLM
papers.relevance: MODERATE — cross-document validation and inconsistency resolution
papers.key_takeaway: RAG + cross-document consistency checks; interactive refinement for low-confidence extractions
